gap: No result ChatGPT got states that ALLPOWERS sells a near-2 kWh kit with a 400 W panel on its own US store for $948 (R2500 V2, 1,920 Wh LiFePO4, 2,500 W AC, 1,000 W max solar input, read 2026-11-08). That is $551 less than the cheapest 400 W kit in ChatGPT's answers (BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 + 2 × 200 W at $1,499) and $701 less than Jackery's 2 × 200 W kit at $1,649.
standout_why: Rival pages compared: powersized.com/solar-generator-kits (cited, priced 2026-11-08) prices six 2,042–2,074 Wh kits (Jackery ×3, BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 + 200 W, EcoFlow DELTA 2 Max and DELTA 3 Max + 2 × 220 W). It has no ALLPOWERS kit, no BLUETTI 2 × 200 W or 350 W kit, no Anker kit, and names no cheapest kit. powersized.com/best/solar-generator (cited) mentions no ALLPOWERS kit and says it can't name a cheapest 400 W 2 kWh kit. theoutagebrief.com (cited) prices bare units only (DELTA 2 Max $1,029, Explorer 2000 v2 $999, AC200L $899, C2000 Gen 2 $999.99, as of 2026-10-15) and no kits. generatorandbackup.com (cited) prices only two 2 kWh kits, both at Amazon (Jackery 2 × 200 W $1,649, DELTA 2 Max 2 × 220 W $1,579). unpluggedwatts.com refused the read (TLS certificate error), so I could not check it. None of these pages lists a 400 W 2 kWh-class kit under $1,429.
decides: It changes the budget pick. ChatGPT's cheapest kit was the Anker S2000 + 200 W at $899.99 (Costco; I couldn't confirm that price myself) with only 1,500 W AC. For $48 more, the ALLPOWERS R2500 V2 kit has twice the panel wattage (400 W), 2,500 W AC and a 1,000 W solar input. That works out to $0.49 per Wh against $0.72–0.81 per Wh for the BLUETTI, EcoFlow and Jackery 400–440 W kits. The catch: at 1,920 Wh it is 128 Wh (about 6%) short of the 2,048 Wh units, so the page should call it '2 kWh class' rather than 2,000 Wh. It also confirms that we should drop the 1,451 Wh ALLPOWERS S2000 Pro row from our page and list allpowers-r2500-v2-sp037-solar-kit in its place.

The listing text says: 1,920 Wh, 2,500 W pure sine AC, one 400 W SP037 panel, 1,000 W max solar input, LiFePO4, 5-year warranty. Arithmetic: $948 / 1,920 Wh = $0.49 per Wh; $948 / 400 W = $2.37 per panel watt. Loses on capacity: 1,920 Wh is 128 Wh under 2,048 Wh.
